rationale: A wins because it knows where the evidence stops. Its strongest line, "Companies Are Wasting an Average of $342,000 a Year on Software They Don't Use," makes the data the story and immediately asks whether the savings were identified or realized. B is livelier, but "Ramp is giving away the software-audit feature — and charging for the approval workflow" sells an unstated pricing fact as if it were in the release. That's how a good angle gets a reporter to stop trusting you.
gaps_in_A: "a payments-native tool with visibility into $80B of actual spend has an intelligence edge that standalone spend-management tools don't" is plausible, but still an inferred competitive claim. It needs executive backing before it becomes pitch language.

"the first public signal of Ramp explicitly turning payment data into procurement intelligence" overstates what the update proves. The launch shows spend scanning; it does not prove a declared platform strategy.

"The Enterprise AI Agent That Insists Humans Stay in the Loop" leans on a design-philosophy read that the facts do not confirm. A correctly asks for proof, but the headline is still ahead of the evidence.
"200 real customers" is probably true, but the update only says a 200-company beta. Don't upgrade beta participants into customers unless Ramp confirms it.
gaps_in_B: "Ramp's new agent cancels your software subscriptions" is wrong. The agent drafts cancellation or renegotiation emails that finance approves; it does not cancel subscriptions on its own.
"The first AI agents in finance departments aren't doing the math" invents a first-mover claim and contradicts the facts. The agent scans spend and flags unused or duplicate seats, which is analysis.

"Ramp is giving away the software-audit feature — and charging for the approval workflow" invents the charging model. The update says an enterprise tier is coming, not that custom approval workflows are the paid wedge.

"at the scale of $80B in annualized purchase volume" risks laundering total Ramp purchase volume into software-spend scale. B notices the problem in proof needs, but the angle still uses the stretch up front.
